# tokens: # Resource — built-in object type for external data sources
# `Resource` and `Entity` are boru's built-in ObjectTypes for naming
# external data sources. They are not registered as words; instead
# `installResourceTypes` (called from `engine.Register`) pushes them
# onto the type stack at startup. So they're available out of the
# box wherever the production registry is loaded.
# Hierarchy:
#   Ideal/Resource           {kind:String}
#       └── Ideal/Resource/Entity   {spec:String, entity:String}
#                                    (inherits kind from Resource)
# Resource is the abstract carrier; `Entity` adds the (`spec`,
# `entity`) coordinates that pin one specific entity within a
# specifier. Instances are produced via `make Entity {…}` (or via
# user-defined types that extend Resource / Entity).
# This file covers:
#   1. The bare type literals — Resource, Entity.
#   2. Inheritance check — Entity is Resource.
#   3. Instantiation via make.
#   4. Field access on instances.
#   5. is checks for parent / sibling types.
#   6. Field validation at make-time.
# Runs against the production boru registry.
# 1. Bare type literals
Resource
note: the bare type literal renders as its name

# tokens: Entity
typeof Resource
note: Resource is a peer Ideal kind (re-rooted off Object)

# tokens: typeof Entity
# 2. Inheritance — Entity is Resource
# `is` between type literals reports whether the LHS type is a
# subtype of the RHS type. Entity declares Resource as parent in
# installResourceTypes, so the check holds.
Entity is Resource
note: Entity inherits from Resource

# tokens: Resource is Resource
note: a type satisfies itself

# tokens: # Sibling types do not satisfy each other.
Entity is Map
Entity is List
# 3. Instantiation via make
# `make Entity {…}` validates the data against Entity's fields
# (kind:String + spec:String + entity:String, with kind inherited
# from Resource). Returns a typed resource instance rendered as
# `Entity{…}`.
make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'voxgig-solardemo' entity:'planet' } typeof
note: the made value's typeof is Entity

# tokens: make Entity { kind:'db' spec:'users' entity:'user' } typeof
# 4. is checks for the made instance
# An Entity instance satisfies Entity AND its parent Resource —
# inheritance flows through `is` for Type values produced by
# `make`.
make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'x' entity:'y' } is Entity
note: is-check matches own type

# tokens: make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'x' entity:'y' } is Resource
note: parent type is also satisfied

# tokens: # Cross-family checks fail.
make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'x' entity:'y' } is List
make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'x' entity:'y' } is Integer
# 5. Field access via dotted accessor
# Entity instances expose `kind`, `spec`, and `entity` as fields
# accessible through the standard `.field` syntax.
( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'voxgig-solardemo' entity:'planet' } ) .kind
( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'voxgig-solardemo' entity:'planet' } ) .spec
( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'voxgig-solardemo' entity:'planet' } ) .entity
# 6. Field validation at make-time
# `make Entity {…}` requires every declared field. Missing fields
# raise an error rather than installing a partially-typed value.
make Entity { }
note: all three fields are required

# tokens: make Entity { kind:'api' }
note: missing spec and entity

# tokens: make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'x' }
note: missing entity

# tokens: # 7. Composition with def
# `def name make Entity {…}` captures an Entity instance for reuse.
# All field accesses and is-checks survive the round-trip through
# the def stack.
def planet ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'solardemo' entity:'planet' } ) planet .kind
def planet ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'solardemo' entity:'planet' } ) planet .entity
def planet (make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'solardemo' entity:'planet' }) planet is Entity
def planet (make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'solardemo' entity:'planet' }) planet is Resource
# 8. Resource and Entity at the type-stack level
# `Resource` and `Entity` are pushed onto the type stack at startup
# (installResourceTypes), so they're always reachable as type
# literals. Subsequent `type NAME …` declarations don't shadow them.
size [ Resource ]
note: the type literal can be wrapped in a list

# tokens: size [ Entity ]
size [ Resource Entity ]
note: both are first-class type-literal values

# tokens: # A user-defined type that USES Resource or Entity as a parent must
# go through a user-named indirection: a bare Resource/Entity type
# literal is not itself accepted as a refine base in the field-shape
# form. Inheriting requires an intermediate user type.
# 9. Resource/Entity instances are flat field-map values
# Resource/Entity have their OWN instance struct (ResourceInstanceInfo),
# distinct from class instances, but share the flat field-map shape, so
# every container-style operation treats them like class instances:
# size, deq (structural), eq (alias identity), convert, struct-util
# projection, typed-def construction, and const rejection.
size ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: an Entity instance sizes to its field count

# tokens: size ( make Resource { kind:'k' } )
note: a Resource instance counts its one field

# tokens: deq ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } ) ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: structurally-equal Entity instances are deq

# tokens: deq ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } ) ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'z' } )
note: differing fields are NOT deq

# tokens: def e ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } ) def f e e f eq
note: two bindings to the SAME instance are eq (alias identity)

# tokens: eq ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } ) ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: distinct instances are NOT eq even with equal fields

# tokens: convert Map ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: Entity projects to its field map

# tokens: convert List ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: Entity projects to its field values

# tokens: # struct-util projection sees the resolved fields (not a debug string).
import "boru:struct-util" StructUtil.items ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: items enumerates Entity fields

# tokens: import "boru:struct-util" StructUtil.setpath ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } ) "entity" "y"
note: setpath preserves the Entity type and other fields

# tokens: # Typed-def parity: `def e:Entity {map}` constructs like `make Entity {map}`.
def e:Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } e .spec
note: def e:Entity {…} constructs a real Entity instance

# tokens: def e:Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } typeof e
note: typed-def yields an Entity instance

# tokens: def e:Resource { kind:'k' } typeof e
note: typed-def also works for the Resource base

# tokens: def e:Entity { kind:'api' } e
note: typed-def enforces the schema (missing spec/entity)

# tokens: # const rejects a mutable Resource instance (parity with class instances).
const ( make Entity { kind:'api' spec:'s' entity:'x' } )
note: a Resource instance cannot pin a const exemplar
